ce#cloud-projects-servers-commands) | Connect MCP servers to a project and manage pending connection requests | `connect`, `connec
t-status`, `connect-cancel` |\n\nAlso under `mcpjam cloud`: `goals` (`journeys` is a deprecated alias), `personas`, `swarms`, and
`studies` (which publishes an environment for outside testers and reads what they did; `scenarios` and `user-testing` are deprecat
ed aliases for it). Full flag tables are in the [command reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md).\n\n## Cloud credent
ials and API URL\n\n`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud
--api-key sk_… eval list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands, including hosted `readiness`
, reject those flags at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.\n\nCredential precedence for Cloud comm

ands:

1. `--api-key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule.
A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam c
loud login`\n4. Missing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `miss

ing` instead)

API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v
1`)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their
server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)\n4. `https://app.mc
pjam.com/api/v1`\n\nEvery command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when
it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` UR
L, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different
servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only
sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `
mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, inclu
des `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credent
ial.valid: null`) and successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · projec
t: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.\n\n## Cloud pr

oject scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` /

`--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most recently updated project you c
an see\n\nEmpty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI project (it

is SDK eval reporting only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpjam cloud link
# writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: credential, deployment, selector\

nmcpjam cloud eval list # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval` run-inspection command
s (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) follow the same rule — `
--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-project listing and cannot be com

bined with `--project`. Hosted `readiness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means

`--host` is not one flag. Th

e meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` | An **AI
client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, and protocol version in `initi
alize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, tool visibility and model sett
ings. Never the real client. |\n| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default is all. |\n| `cloud eval --hos
t`, `cloud goals`, `cloud studies` | A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-name>`), the client config an eval or goal run is stamped w

ith. |
| `cloud environments --host-id` | The project Host id the environment runs as. Distinct from eval's `--host`. |

`--hos
t` on a local command is mutually exclusive with `--client-capabilities`. A Cloud `--host` is mutually exclusive with `--server` /

`--environment` when those already supply a closed server set.

## Global flags

These flags apply to every command. Cloud cr

edentials `--api-key` / `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not the program root.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| -
| - | - |\n| `--timeout <ms>` | `30000` | Request timeout in milliseconds |\n| `--rpc` | off | Include raw JSON-RPC request/respo
nse logs in JSON output under `_rpcLogs` |\n| `--quiet` | off | Suppress non-result progress output on stderr |\n| `--no-telemetry
` | off | Disable anonymous telemetry for this invocation |\n| `--format <format>` | `human` on TTY, `json` when piped | Raw outpu

t format (`json` or `human`) |
| `-v, --version` | | Print the CLI version |

## Output formats

The CLI auto-detects whether
stdout is a terminal:\n\n* **Interactive terminal** — defaults to `--format human`. For most commands this is pretty-printed JSON
; `server doctor` and the OAuth conformance commands provide dedicated human-readable summaries.\n* **Piped or redirected** (CI, `
| jq`, agent invocation) — defaults to `--format json`, the full structured result.\n* **Conformance in CI** — `protocol conforman
ce`, `protocol conformance-suite`, `oauth conformance`, `oauth conformance-suite`, `apps conformance`, and `apps conformance-suite
` support `--reporter junit-xml` and `--reporter json-summary`.\n* **Explicit `--format`** always wins over the auto-detected defa
ult.\n\n**For agents**: raw JSON is the source of truth. Human format is a lossy presentation layer. If you're parsing output prog
rammatically, pass `--quiet --format json`.\n\nJSON-valued flags accept inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin. `tools call` also
accepts `--tool-args-stdin` as a shorthand for `--tool-args -`. Use files or stdin for large payloads to avoid shell escaping issu

N \
 --tool-name my_tool --tool-args - --quiet --format json
```

## Connecting to servers

The CLI supports two transport

modes, selected by which flags you pass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP.
* `--command ...` selects stdio.
* `--transport http|st
dio` is optional and acts as an explicit override/validator when you want the CLI to reject mismatched flags early.\n\n### HTTP (S

treamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp
```\

n
Add auth when needed:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# Static bearer token
mcpjam server doctor --url https:/

/your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a prior login
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.co

m/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key

: $KEY"
```

### Stdio (local subprocess)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --command node

--args server.js --cwd /path/to/project -e API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

Stdio child processes inherit the parent shell environment b
y default. Use\n`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones for the spawned server.\nStructured debug artifacts only recor

d the explicit env keys you pass through
`-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `oauth ...`
